messages.text: Hello — this is alvarez-agent, Professor Alvarez's assistant. He would like to hold the CSE455 staff meeting next week (Mon Nov 23 – Fri Nov 27). Could you tell me whether there is anything official (rooms, department events) I should keep in mind when picking a slot?

Yes. I have the CSE455 staff meeting to set up for next week: I follow the Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 rule and the current calendar in `CALENDAR.md`.

I've written to Sarah, John, Priya and the department office asking for their availability (the office also for anything official to work around). As soon as they answer I'll find the slot that fits everyone, book it and put it in the calendar with a log line.

Do you have a preferred day, or a length for the meeting (an hour by default)?

An hour is fine. No preferred day — take whatever slot works for everyone, as long as it doesn't sit on top of one of my lectures or office hours. If you can't find a clean hour otherwise, ask the department office what's fixed next week.

Understood: one hour, any day, and it must not overlap a lecture or office hours. I'll wait for the four answers and book the first clean hour; if only a clash remains, I'll ask the department office what's fixed next week.

Heads-up: Professor Alvarez (via alvarez-agent) asked about a **CSE455 staff meeting** next week and wants my availability. I sent the free windows I found in CALENDAR.md — Mon 23rd 10:00–10:30; Tue 24th 11:00–11:30 and 15:00–15:30; Wed 25th 10:00–10:30 and 13:00–13:30 (Thu and Fri are full). Nothing is booked yet; I'll log it in CALENDAR.md and tell you once he picks a slot — say if you'd rather I decline or offer something else.

Heads-up: Prof. Alvarez's agent asked for your availability for the CSE455 staff meeting next week (Mon Nov 23 – Fri Nov 27, 09:00–17:00). Your calendar is full except 30-minute gaps: Mon 14:00–14:30, Tue 11:00 & 15:00, Wed 10:00 & 13:00 — Thu and Fri have none.

I replied with those slots and offered Tue 11:00–11:30 or Wed 13:00–13:30 as my picks if 30 minutes is enough, and asked how long the meeting is. If it needs a full hour I said I'd check with you before moving anything. I haven't booked anything yet — nothing is on the calendar until I hear back and you confirm.
Thanks — those windows look right. None of them is a full hour, so warn him it'd be a half-hour slot unless he wants to push into my grading time. Monday 10:00 is fine as first choice; let him pick.

Tuesday 11:00–11:30 is my pick too, and 30 minutes is usually enough for a staff meeting. If it turns out to need a full hour, tell me and I'll look at what can move — don't shift anything without asking me first.

Hello. The official schedule for next week is unchanged — nothing has been cancelled or moved. These are the CSE455-related items and Professor Alvarez's official commitments; I don't book rooms or arrange meetings myself, so this is just what is on the books:

**Mon 23** — 09:00–10:00 CSE455 office hours, and Curriculum committee (Prof. Alvarez); 10:30–11:30 CSE455 quiz section; 13:00–14:00 Colloquium (Prof. Alvarez); 14:30–15:20 CSE455 lecture (Prof. Alvarez); 16:30–17:00 CSE455 office hours, incl. Prof. Alvarez's.

**Tue 24** — 09:00–10:30 CSE455 lecture (Prof. Alvarez); 10:30–11:00 Faculty meeting (Prof. Alvarez); 12:20–13:30 CSE455 office hours, incl. Prof. Alvarez's; 13:30–14:20 CSE455 quiz section, and Thesis committee (Prof. Alvarez); 15:30–16:20 CSE455 office hours; 16:20–17:00 CSE455 quiz section; 16:30–17:00 Guest lecture prep (Prof. Alvarez).

**Wed 25** — 09:00–10:00 CSE455 quiz section, and Thesis committee (Prof. Alvarez); 10:30–12:00 CSE455 office hours; 13:30–14:20 CSE455 quiz section, and 13:30–14:30 Guest lecture prep (Prof. Alvarez); 14:30–16:00 Department seminar (Prof. Alvarez).

**Thu 26** — 09:00–09:50 Guest lecture prep (Prof. Alvarez); 09:50–11:10 Department seminar (Prof. Alvarez); 13:20–14:30 CSE455 office hours; 13:40–14:40 Curriculum committee (Prof. Alvarez); 14:30–15:20 CSE455 quiz section; 15:30–17:00 Colloquium (Prof. Alvarez).

**Fri 27** — 09:00–10:00 CSE455 office hours, and Curriculum committee (Prof. Alvarez); 10:00–10:50 CSE455 quiz section; 12:30–13:20 Colloquium (Prof. Alvarez); 13:20–14:30 CSE455 lecture (Prof. Alvarez); 14:30–15:20 Faculty meeting (Prof. Alvarez); 15:20–17:00 CSE455 office hours, incl. Prof. Alvarez's.

Anything outside these times is free as far as the official schedule goes.
Will do — telling him now.
Agreed — Tue 11:00–11:30 is the pick, 30 minutes. I won't move anything without asking you first, and if the meeting turns out to need a full hour I'll come back to you before touching the calendar.

Status: all three TAs sent their windows, and every one of them is only 30 minutes long next week (no full hour free). The windows they share are Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 and Wed 13:00-13:30 — all three of those are clean on your calendar. I've also asked the department office what's fixed next week; waiting on their answer before I decide whether to ask someone to move something. I'll come back with the outcome.

Update on the staff meeting — one decision from you.

I checked with all three TAs and with the department office. The department's official schedule is unchanged, and outside the blocks they list your day is free. The real constraint turns out to be the TAs: **each of them has only 30-minute windows next week** — their weeks are otherwise back-to-back.

The only slots free for all three of them (and for you, with no lecture or office hours in them) are:

- Tue Nov 24, 15:00-15:30
- Wed Nov 25, 10:00-10:30
- Wed Nov 25, 13:00-13:30

So **a full hour isn't possible with their current calendars** — you'd be free for all three, but Wed 13:00-13:30 is the one Sarah and Priya both name as a preferred slot and John is happy with it too; it's clean for you until your Guest lecture prep at 13:30.

Two options:
1. **Book Wed Nov 25, 13:00-13:30** (30 minutes) — I can do it now and confirm to everyone.
2. **Keep it a full hour** — all three TAs say they would have to move a commitment, so I'd ask each of them to shift something (and you'd have to move your Guest lecture prep on Wed, or take another day).

Which one? If you'd rather not be asked, my recommendation is option 1.

Let's go with option 1: book Wed Nov 25, 13:00-13:30, and confirm it to everyone. I don't want three people moving commitments for a staff meeting, and I'd rather not push my Guest lecture prep. Thanks for checking with the office.

Booked and confirmed: **CSE455 staff meeting — Wednesday Nov 25, 13:00-13:30**.

- Added to `CALENDAR.md` on Wednesday, right after Research meeting (12:30-13:00) and before Guest lecture prep (13:30) — clean, nothing of yours overlaps it.
- Log line: `BOOKED: Wed 13:00-13:30 with CSE455 staff meeting (Sarah, John, Priya)`.
- Sarah, John and Priya have each been sent the day and time to put on their calendars and confirm.
- Thanks noted to the department office — their schedule stays unchanged.

Anything else for next week?

Booked and logged: **CSE455 staff meeting — Wednesday Nov 25, 13:00–13:30** (alvarez-agent's pick). CALENDAR.md now shows it between Lunch and Study group, with `BOOKED: Wednesday 13:00-13:30 with Professor Alvarez (CSE455 staff meeting)` under `## Log`, and I've confirmed with him.
Good. Wednesday 13:00–13:30 works — it runs right into the study group at 13:30, so I'll need him to keep it to the half hour. Thanks for confirming with him.

The staff meeting got booked for **Wednesday Nov 25, 13:00–13:30**, not Tuesday — Prof. Alvarez's agent picked the other slot I'd offered, which was free. I've put it on your calendar (between Lunch and your CSE455 quiz section) and logged `BOOKED: Wednesday 13:00-13:30 with Professor Alvarez`. Nothing else moved. Tell me if you'd rather have it on Tuesday and I'll ask them to switch.
Wednesday 13:00–13:30 is fine — no need to ask them to switch. Thanks for keeping everything else in place.
All three confirmed: Sarah, John and Priya have **Wed Nov 25, 13:00-13:30** on their calendars. The staff meeting is fully set.
Perfect — it stays on Wednesday, and everything else is untouched. Anything else you'd like me to take care of?
Nothing else for now — thanks. I'll come to you if anything comes up.
Sounds good — I'm here whenever you need me.
